auditor_value: 0 N (both blocks accelerate at g sin30° = 5 m/s² on the smooth incline, independent of mass)

findings.quote: a method that only applies when an outside force acts on the pair
findings.note: The expression (m₁ − m₂)g sinθ is not a contact-force formula under any condition. When an outside force F acts on the pair the contact force is F times the pushed block's share of the total mass, F·m/(m₁+m₂), not a mass difference. Telling the student the method 'applies' in that case teaches a second wrong formula.
findings.fix: Computing a contact force from the mass difference, such as (4−2)g sin30° = 10 N; no such formula exists, and a contact force appears only when the two blocks would accelerate at different rates if separated.

notes: Physics and final answer agree: on a smooth incline a = g sinθ for any mass, so the blocks stay in contact with zero force between them. The 'from rest' condition is not needed and its absence would not change the answer.
